transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I'm Dennis. I guess I'm here because of my eating. What really made me come in today is that... well, once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some switch. I just keep going, even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already. I just can't seem to stop myself once it starts.
After one of these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you do anything afterward to try to 'undo' it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot to compensate?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything. I just... I usually just feel really full and kind of bad about it, but I don't try to get rid of the food or work it off.
On average, how often do these episodes of feeling out of control while eating happen, and how many months has this been going on?

I'd say... since early in the semester, it’s been happening most weeks. Usually it's just one night, but sometimes it's two if I have a lot of deadlines or if food is just piling up in the apartment. So, yeah, I guess that pattern has been pretty steady for at least the last three or four months now.
During these episodes, do you notice yourself eating much faster than usual, or eating alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah, I definitely eat a lot faster during those times. Like, I'll just be standing at my desk, maybe in between finishing some homework and starting up a game, and I'll just eat... really fast. I barely even taste it, honestly. I'll just look down and realize all the food is gone, and it only took a few minutes. As for eating alone... yeah, I usually do it when my roommates aren't around. I wouldn't want them to see me putting away that much food that quickly.
Would you say these episodes cause you a lot of distress or upset you significantly, beyond just feeling physically uncomfortable afterward?

Yeah, it definitely does. Afterward, I just feel really embarrassed and... kind of grossed out with myself, honestly. I mean, I'm usually pretty disciplined with my classes and my robotics stuff, so when this happens... it really bothers me because it just makes me feel like I'm completely not in control.
